subject: Renewal discussion — reprofiling GPU reserve for Q2 runway
messages:
From: Elena Park <elena@cloudscale.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
Cc: Javier Morales <javier.morales@cloudscale.com>
Date: 2027-03-18T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Renewal + capacity add — urgent runway request

Vivek,

Quick note ahead of the renewal conversation next week. We saw a sustained uplift in inference traffic across Feb→Mar tied to two new internal products. High-level figures: average committed pool utilization ~72% over last 30 days, 95th percentile sustained peaks hitting 88–92% for 60–120 minute windows. Attached is a CSV with per-day GPU-hours and a short chart.

We are approaching the end of our current committed tranche (expires end of May). Can Redwood support either (a) a short-term top-up of ~16 reserved GPUs for the next 12 months while we evaluate, or (b) reprofiling our commit to a slightly larger baseline to reduce throttling?

Key constraints from procurement: 1) minimal operational disruption, 2) prefer a single contract amendment vs monthly swaps, 3) lead time is a factor (we need capacity provisioned within ~2 weeks if possible).

I'm looping Javier (procurement) for timing. Can you confirm options, high-level pricing, and any lead-time implications?

Thanks — Elena
Elena Park
Head of Data Platforms | CloudScale Solutions
Attachments: usage_report_feb-mar.csv (CSV, 1.2MB)

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
To: Elena Park <elena@cloudscale.com>
Cc: Javier Morales <javier.morales@cloudscale.com>, laura_bennett@redwood.com, rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
Date: 2027-03-18T11:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal + capacity add — urgent runway request

Elena — thanks for the data, that CSV was helpful. High level: we can support both approaches. Two quick notes up front: lead time for reserved capacity warm-up is typically 7–14 business days for a new tranche, and reprofiling an existing commit is possible but has contractual and billing implications depending on remaining term.

Proposed next steps (short):
- Internal alignment (we'll scope pricing + lead time) — I'll loop in Rishi and Laura.
- Quick 30-min sync with you + Javier to confirm preferred option (top-up vs reprofiling).
- We'll produce a 1-page proposal with estimated monthly delta, term options, and a recommended fallback (burst pool) if you want a non-committed cushion.

If it helps, initial thinking: a 16-GPU top-up for 12 months is the lowest-friction path and gets you immediate runway. Reprofiling to a larger baseline (e.g., move from 80 -> 96 GPUs equivalent) looks better unit-cost-wise but we'd want to model usage volatility to avoid overcommitting.

Available slots for a call: Thu 3/18 3:00–4:00pm PT or Fri 3/19 10:00–11:00am PT.

— Vivek
Vivek Kulkarni
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference
Redwood Inference

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
To: laura_bennett@redwood.com, rishi_malhotra@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: 2027-03-19T09:40:00-07:00
Subject: Internal: CloudScale renewal — propose options and ask for numbers

Team — quick internal thread after Elena's ask. Attached I added an annotated utilization snapshot (annotated_util_chart.png). TL;DR: CloudScale is at ~72% baseline, with daily peak windows that push them above 85–90%. They need runway by mid-late May.

Please advise:
- Rishi: operationally, can we provision a 16-GPU reserve within 10 business days and serve as a standalone tranche? Any migration steps for their fleet?
- Marissa: rough pricing scenarios (monthly delta for top-up; delta/discounts for reprofiling to a 96 baseline; and a burst-pool/overage rate) so I can present clear trade-offs.
- Laura: any contractual gotchas with an amendment vs a rewrite if they ask for 18-month term?

Goal: get a one-pager by EOD today so I can send to Elena before our call.

Thanks — Vivek
Attachments: annotated_util_chart.png

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>, laura_bennett@redwood.com, rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
Date: 2027-03-19T15:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Internal: CloudScale renewal — pricing scenarios (draft)

Vivek / team — draft numbers below. These are headline figures only, finance will reconcile but should be within <3%: 

Option A — Short-term top-up (low friction)
- 16 reserved GPUs (same GPU family as their current commit)
- Term: 12 months (starts on provision date)
- Lead time: ~10 business days to provision and validate
- Commercial: +$46k/month commit delta; 10% credit applied to renewal if they sign within 30 days

Option B — Reprofile baseline (unit-cost efficient)
- Increase committed baseline from 80 -> 96 GPUs equivalent
- Term: 18 months (preferred by CS)
- Commercial: +$35k/month (lower per-GPU rate than top-up because of longer term) + 15% renewal discount; onboarding credit $10k applied to first invoice
- Lead time: 7–12 business days (may require scheduling to avoid maintenance windows)

Option C — Burst / pay-as-you-go cushion
- No long-term commit; burst pool available on demand up to 24 GPUs
- Unit cost higher than commit; good as a temporary buffer but will increase monthly OPEX if used heavily

Notes: provisioning an additional reserved tranche will require a quick capacity reservation with infra scheduling; finance prefers Option B from margin perspective but will accept A if CloudScale needs minimal change management. Attached a 1-page proposal PDF (proposal_summary_Q2.pdf) you can send to CS.

— Marissa
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
Attachments: proposal_summary_Q2.pdf

From: Elena Park <elena@cloudscale.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
Cc: Javier Morales <javier.morales@cloudscale.com>, laura_bennett@redwood.com, rishi_malhotra@redwood.com, marissa@redwood.com
Date: 2027-03-21T16:07:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal + capacity add — decision and next steps

Vivek / team — thanks for the quick turnaround and clear options. After internal procurement review we want to proceed with Option B (reprofile baseline 80 -> 96 GPUs equivalent) on an 18-month term. The lower unit cost plus the onboarding credit makes sense for our forecast.

Next steps from our side: Javier (procurement) will receive the DocuSign packet and countersign. Please route contract amendment + new SOW to javier.morales@cloudscale.com. We would like provisioning to start immediately after countersignature — target start date no later than 2027-04-05 if possible.

Couple of asks:
- Can you include a clause that allows a one-time mid-term review at month 9 to adjust burst allowances?
- Confirm lead time once DocuSign is returned so we can align internal release schedules.

CCing Javier to confirm procurement timing.

Best — Elena
Elena Park
Head of Data Platforms | CloudScale Solutions
